questions.question: What structural interpretation did the authors give for the Fe species in AuFeHS, combining XANES and EXAFS observations?

options.A: Fe was mainly metallic in large particles, with a Fe–Fe shell near the foil distance
options.B: Fe was atomically dispersed and lower-valent than FeHS, with neighboring oxygen shells at about 1.94 and 2.11 Å
options.C: Fe was present exclusively as FeOOH clusters coordinated by Au atoms
options.D: Fe formed a spinel phase with no oxygen coordination and a 3.7 Å Fe–Fe distance

questions.rationale: The Fe edge showed no Fe–Fe interaction; its first shell was two neighboring O shells, while spectroscopy indicated reduced-valent Fe in AuFeHS.
questions.evidence_quote: The peak at ~1.5Å corresponds to two neighbouring O shells with C.N. of 3 at 1.94 Å and 2.11Å.

questions.question: Which XPS/XANES-derived explanation links Au to stabilization of the catalytically relevant iron state?

options.A: Au0 oxidizes Fe3+ to FeOOH, the species assigned to peroxide activation
options.B: Cationic Auδ+ was proposed to donate charge and stabilize low-valent Fe3−δ+
options.C: Auδ+ removes Na from silica, converting Fe into metallic nanoparticles
options.D: Au0 accepts charge from Fe3−δ+, preventing its interaction with methane

questions.rationale: The paper connects the cationic Au component to charge donation and stabilization of reduced iron, which can activate methane and peroxide.
questions.evidence_quote: A higher binding energy peak ~ 85 eV (4f 7/2) establishing cationic (Au δ+ ) species shows a possible charge donation and stabilization of the Fe 3-δ+ species.

questions.question: What were the fitted iron-oxide contributions reported for AuFeHS from Fe-edge linear-combination fitting?
questions.rationale: Linear-combination fitting of the AuFeHS Fe-edge data assigned 72% contribution to Fe3O4 and 28% to FeO.
questions.evidence_quote: by linear combination fitting (LCF), we could see that it has a 72% contribution of Fe3O4 and 28% FeO

questions.question: At what Au and Fe loadings was the best-performing AuFeHS catalyst optimized, and what measured metal fractions did the authors report?

options.A: 0.5 wt% Au and 0.2 wt% Fe, measured as 0.46 wt% Au and 0.23 wt% Fe
options.B: 0.2 wt% Au and 0.5 wt% Fe, measured as 0.46 wt% Fe and 0.23 wt% Au
options.C: 0.23 wt% Au and 0.46 wt% Fe, measured as 0.5 wt% Fe and 0.2 wt% Au
options.D: 0.46 wt% Au and 0.23 wt% Fe, measured as 0.2 wt% Fe and 0.5 wt% Au

questions.rationale: The optimized nominal composition was 0.2Au/0.5Fe; ICP-OES reported 0.23 wt% Au and 0.46 wt% Fe.
questions.evidence_quote: had an optimum Fe concentration of 0.46 wt % and Au concentration of 0.23 wt %

questions.question: Which comparison most directly supports a special role for the hydrophobic support beyond simply carrying the two metals?

options.A: AuFe on SBA-15 produced 0.78 mmol/gcat methanol versus 0.30 and 0.15 for Fe- and Au-SBA-15
options.B: AuFeHS had 392 m²/g surface area, while the monometallic samples had no measurable area
options.C: AuFeHS produced 224 mmol/gFe+Au continuously, whereas AuFe on SBA-15 produced only 111 mmol/gFe+Au
options.D: Hydrophobic silica gave no product, while FeHS and AuHS produced identical yields

questions.rationale: The silica-support comparison under optimized conditions showed 111 mmol/gFe+Au on SBA-15 versus the much higher AuFeHS yield.
questions.evidence_quote: Au and Fe supported on SBA-15 gave only 111 mmol/gFe+Au methanol under optimized conditions

questions.question: How did adding CO alter the product distribution in the batch methane oxidation experiment?

options.A: It suppressed liquid products and made CO2 the sole product
options.B: It switched the main liquid product to acetic acid, with methanol remaining as a minor oxygenate
options.C: It increased methanol selectivity to 100% while eliminating CO2
options.D: It changed the reaction from peroxide oxidation to oxygen-driven methanol synthesis

questions.rationale: With CO co-feed, acetic acid was the principal liquid oxygenate and methanol was also detected at much lower yield.
questions.evidence_quote: there was a selectivity switch and acetic acid was formed as the main product with a yield of 3403 µmol/gcat

questions.question: Which continuous-flow comparison did the authors use to establish Au–Fe synergy on hydrophobic silica?

options.A: AuFeHS gave 224 mmol/gFe+Au in 4 h, compared with 24.2 mmol/gFe for FeHS and 12 mmol/gAu for AuHS
options.B: AuFeHS gave 1666 mmol/gFe+Au in 30 min, compared with 285 mmol/gFe for FeHS and 47.6 mmol/gAu for AuHS
options.C: AuFeHS gave 422 mmol/gcat/h, compared with 1.81 for FeHS and 0.081 for AuHS
options.D: AuFeHS gave 648 µmol/gcat acetic acid, whereas FeHS and AuHS gave no methanol

questions.rationale: The 4-hour atmospheric-pressure continuous test reported 224 mmol/gFe+Au for AuFeHS, above either monometallic catalyst.
questions.evidence_quote: FeHS catalyst produced 24.2 mmol/gFe of methanol while an outstanding product yield of 224 mmol/gFe+Au was reported in the case of AuFeHS.

questions.question: What result from isotope tracing specifically argues that methanol's methyl group came from methane rather than the hydrophobic support?

options.A: A 3.3 ppm multiplet in the 1H NMR appeared in CD4 labeling, and 2H/13C NMR also confirmed labeled methanol
options.B: The 3.3 ppm signal disappeared under N2 feed, while the 13C spectrum showed unlabeled methanol
options.C: CD4 labeling shifted the acetic-acid carbonyl signal, but did not alter methanol spectra
options.D: The 1H spectrum showed no methyl signal, so the authors inferred methane was the carbon source indirectly

questions.rationale: The CD4 experiment produced the diagnostic multiplet and labeled methanol was further supported by deuterium and carbon NMR.
questions.evidence_quote: The peak at 3.3 ppm showed multiplet in 1 H NMR spectra, confirming that the methyl group in the alcohol originated from CD4 rather than any other ligands from the support

questions.question: Which active-site sequence did the authors propose for converting methane to methanol and then acetic acid?

options.A: Au0 abstracts hydrogen to form CH3OH directly; Fe3+ inserts CO into methanol
options.B: Lewis acid sites form a methane C–H sigma complex; low-valent Fe forms CH3 and OH radicals, enabling methanol and facile CO insertion
options.C: Na sites cleave methane homolytically; Auδ+ couples two methyl radicals before Fe oxidizes them
options.D: FeOOH produces methyl cations, while Au nanoparticles convert peroxide into molecular oxygen

questions.rationale: The proposed mechanism assigns methane activation to acidic sites and reduced Fe, then notes that the resulting radicals favor methanol formation and CO insertion.
questions.evidence_quote: The activated C-H sigma complex gets converted to CH3 radical on the low valent Fe 3-δ+ sites. Once the CH3 and OH radicals are formed, methanol formation, facile CO insertion, and acetic acid generation become easy.

questions.question: What caveat did the authors explicitly leave unresolved about the catalytic formulation?

options.A: Whether gold particle size controls the reaction was unresolved because all samples had identical Au sizes
options.B: The role of Na and Lewis-acid sites in the overall partial-oxidation reaction remained to be explored
options.C: Whether methane rather than support ligands supplies methanol carbon remained uncertain after labeling
options.D: The authors could not determine whether Fe was present in the catalyst after reaction

questions.rationale: The discussion says these two support-related features may matter but their role was outside the study's scope.
questions.evidence_quote: the role of Na and Lewis acid sites in the overall POM reaction is worth exploring and is beyond the scope of this study.
